opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company — this quarter it also carried the one-off Leadership Experience 2025 gathering of more than 14,000 store leaders.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Wear and tear on coffeehouses, roasteries and equipment.

opex.name: Restructuring & impairments
opex.note: Restructuring under 'Back to Starbucks' — small this quarter; the big store-closure charges landed the following quarter.

follow100Note: Starbucks reports in tenths of a million; the figures on this page are rounded to whole $M.
footerNote: Reported operating income of $936M includes $57M of income from equity investees, shown here in Other income. Net earnings of $558M are essentially all attributable to Starbucks (noncontrolling interests took $0.2M).

kpis.label: Revenue
kpis.note: to $9.5B, a record (+3% in constant currencies)

oneTimers: A non-recurring investment in Leadership Experience 2025 — a three-day conference for more than 14,000 North American store leaders — plus a discrete tax item reduced EPS by $0.11 in total; much of the conference cost sits in general & administrative expense, which rose 18% to $677M.
Restructuring charges were $21M under 'Back to Starbucks' — minor next to the $755M of store-closure charges that landed the following quarter.
otherDetail: Income from equity investees of $57M and $26M of interest and other income, less $142M of interest expense.

segments.name: North America
segments.note: Coffeehouses in the U.S. and Canada — comparable store sales fell 2%, with 3% fewer transactions partly offset by a 1% higher average ticket.

segments.name: International
segments.note: Coffeehouses outside North America — comparable sales were flat, with China up 2% on 6% more transactions.

segments.name: Channel Development
segments.note: Packaged coffee and ready-to-drink drinks sold in grocery and convenience stores — growth came from the Global Coffee Alliance.

segments.name: Corporate & other
segments.note: Small leftover businesses and unallocated items.

takeaways.text: Global comparable store sales fell 2% on 2% fewer transactions, partly offset by a 1% higher average ticket. North America comps fell 2% (U.S. −2%); International was flat, with China up 2% on 6% more transactions.
takeaways.title: Comps were still negative

takeaways.text: GAAP EPS was $0.49 and non-GAAP EPS $0.50. Management said the Leadership Experience 2025 investment for 14,000+ store leaders, plus a discrete tax item, cut EPS by $0.11 in the aggregate.
takeaways.title: One-offs cost 11 cents of EPS

takeaways.text: Starbucks opened 308 net new stores in the quarter, ending with 41,097 — 53% company-operated and 47% licensed. New stores helped revenue grow 4% to a record $9.5B.
takeaways.title: Still opening stores

verdict: Starbucks grew revenue 4% to a record $9.5B, but comparable sales fell 2% and profit dropped 47% to $558M as it poured money into store staffing and a one-off leadership conference under 'Back to Starbucks'.
